title: Zechariah the Prophet
lead: Zechariah, a priest and prophet who began to preach in 520 BC, shared Haggai's call to rebuild the Temple. His night visions, his words to Zerubbabel and Joshua, and the later oracles of the book that bears his name are among the Old Testament passages most used by the Gospels.

sections.b: Zechariah 1:1 calls him "son of Berechiah, son of Iddo"; Ezra names him by his better-known grandfather (Ezra 5:1; Ezra 6:14), the head of a priestly family that came back from Babylon (Nehemiah 12:4; Nehemiah 12:16). His visions, dated from 520 to 518 BC, show the high priest Joshua cleansed (Zechariah 3), the lampstand and two olive trees (Zechariah 4), and the promise that "Zerubbabel's hands founded this house, and his hands will finish it" (Zechariah 4:9, translated fresh). He also speaks of "a man whose name is Branch" who will build the LORD's temple (Zechariah 6:12, translated fresh). Matthew quotes the later chapters at Jesus' entry into Jerusalem (Matthew 21:5, from Zechariah 9:9). He is not the Zechariah son of Jehoiada stoned in the Temple court (2 Chronicles 24:20–22), though Matthew 23:35 joins the two names.
